lab.providerMode: Local DocuSign protocol stand-in from rewalk/signing/server.mjs and signing-overlay.yml (unchanged), applied by up-r2.sh. No real provider account and no real credentials. The RSA key and Connect secret were generated in memory per run.
lab.lifecycle: The lab was created and seeded once for attempt 1, destroyed, created and seeded again for the counted run, and destroyed after the run (no containers or volumes remain).

diffFindings: No file under apps/api/src/lib/signing, apps/api/src/pipeline, apps/api/src/modules/contract-envelopes, signing-connector, signing-webhook, packages/db, apps/web/src/components/approvals, or apps/web/src/routes/contract-* changed in the range.

attempts.detail: Main phase on the first sign-r2 lab, started about 13 seconds after the stand-in overlay restarted the app. legal_team_member passed its 16 steps. The administrator step 'With the connector enabled, Send for signature stays absent when no primary Document is set and appears when one is' timed out after 30 s waiting for the Contract sections Approvals link on C-38, and the 15 later administrator steps did not run. A probe right after opened C-36, C-37 and C-38 as Daniel Okafor, and the Approvals link appeared in 135 to 242 ms, with no container restart. I judged it a transient load delay. I destroyed the lab, built a fresh one, warmed the app, and ran the whole main phase again. That run is the counted one.
Counted run: main 35 of 35 steps passed, polling 2 of 2 passed, note check 1 of 1 passed.

observations: Polling phase: the script counts the webhook note right after the send answers and does not assert the count. It read 0 here and 1 in round 1. approvals-signing-card.tsx is unchanged. note-check-r2.mjs waited for the Out for signature row in Polling mode and found the note once, still there after reload, and gone after a void. The article sentence 'The note under a live row still says that status arrives by webhook in both modes.' holds.

Polling phase: the record read Signed 0.5 minutes after the provider completion (round 1: 4.0 minutes). The first worker sweep happened to fall soon after the send. The article says an update 'can take about 15 to 20 minutes', and this faster result does not contradict it.
limitations: Local DocuSign protocol stand-in only. It cannot show Sign Here placement, white text, or free-form fallback. docusign.ts is unchanged, so the live-provider evidence and the /sig/ limitations in the current evidence still apply.
One counted run per phase. Browser contexts were 1280x1800 CSS px, headless Chromium.
